transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2027-08-18
- Time: 15:00 - 15:57 UTC
- Duration: ~57 minutes
- Attendees: Avery Chen, Marcus Patel, Dana Liu (Redwood); Priya Shah, Ethan Mora, Lindsey Park, Rashid Karim (Gossamer)

Summary:
Quick kickoff for the onboarding playbook and network/security intake. Align on host modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private), initial pilot scope, benchmark window, security artifacts and next steps. Several questions about VPC peering, KMS, and canary rollouts.

Topics:
- Deployment modes and tradeoffs (latency vs cost)
- Networking and VPC peering details
- Compliance (SOC2/SAML/KMS)
- Pilot scope and success criteria
- Benchmarks and performance plan

00:00 Speaker 1 (Avery): All right hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Avery from Redwood, I'm the account owner for Gossamer, we'll do quick intros and then Marcus will walk through the onboarding playbook, Dana will cover the benchmark plan and infra checklist.
00:18 Speaker 2 (Priya): Hi I'm Priya Shah, head of ML at Gossamer, happy to be here.
00:25 Speaker 3 (Lindsey): Lindsey Park, CTO, I'll be dropping in on network questions.
00:32 Speaker 4 (Ethan): Ethan Mora, platform engineer, I'll take the VPC and infra action items.
00:38 Speaker 5 (Rashid): Rashid Karim, security, SOC 2 and audit side for us.
00:44 Speaker 1 (Avery): Great, thanks. Marcus do you want to kick us off with the playbook?
01:02 Speaker 6 (Marcus): Yup, thanks Avery. So the high level we run new customers through a 3-week launchpad: week zero is network and access, week one is pilot integration and smoke tests, week two is performance ramp and canary. We call out optional dedicated capacity if you need predictable latency.
01:28 Speaker 2 (Priya): Quick question — for the pilot, can you do both hosted API and private in parallel? We want to compare latency and cost.
01:36 Speaker 6 (Marcus): You can, yes. Most customers start hosted for speed then move to dedicated or private for production. We can do parallel runs but there are a few things: if you run private you need to set up the control plane access and KMS/HSM hooks, and for dedicated we need capacity commit details.
01:58 Speaker 7 (Dana): Also worth noting that our runtime supports automatic prefix caching and batching; if your prompt distribution has long shared prefixes you'll see big token-cost wins without latency regressions.
02:17 Speaker 3 (Lindsey): When you say private, is that VPC peering or something like a private appliance?
02:25 Speaker 7 (Dana): For VPC-based private we do a customer-managed VPC with peering or transit gateway. There's also an on-prem package for air-gapped if you need it, though that's heavier. We'll share network diagrams.
02:44 Speaker 4 (Ethan): For peering what's the egress pattern? Do we need specific firewall rules outbound?
02:50 Speaker 6 (Marcus): You need outbound to Redwood control plane IPs for initial provisioning, and then traffic is routed via the private link. We'll send the exact CIDR ranges. For dedicated capacity there may be NAT requirements depending on your subneting.
03:11 Speaker 5 (Rashid): On encryption — our legal team requires customer-managed keys. How does KMS integration work?
03:21 Speaker 7 (Dana): We support customer KMS for model keys and also envelope encryption. For some on-prem flows you can use HSM. We'll attach the KMS integration doc; it's in the security pack.
03:34 Speaker 2 (Priya): Good. Also latency — our SLA target is 50–100ms p50 for short prompts, is that realistic?
03:44 Speaker 6 (Marcus): Depends on model and quantization. For smaller quantized variants we can get low p50s but at some cost to quality. We should plan a bench week to measure p50 and p95 on your actual prompt set.
04:02 Speaker 2 (Priya): Ok let's schedule that.
04:08 Speaker 1 (Avery): We'll tentatively pencil Sep 6-10 for the benchmark window unless that conflicts with your schedule.
04:14 Speaker 3 (Lindsey): That works.
04:18 Speaker 8 (Priya) (crosstalk): Sorry —
04:22 Speaker 4 (Ethan): On network — I'll need the VPC CIDRs and the egress rules contact by next Tuesday, 8/23.
04:32 Speaker 1 (Avery): Noted. We'll put that in the action items.
04:40 Speaker 5 (Rashid): On audit logs, can you confirm retention and whether they include per-request metadata?
04:48 Speaker 7 (Dana): Yes we capture per-request traces and token-level cost breakdowns in the Console; retention tiers are an add-on but we'll include default retention and sample logs in the pack.
05:02 Speaker 2 (Priya): We'll want to obfuscate PII in logs — is that standard?
05:09 Speaker 7 (Dana): We have redaction and prefix-kv cache controls; if you need guaranteed non-retention we can configure it for the pilot.
05:24 Speaker 1 (Avery): Great. Marcus, can you walk through the high-level rollout plan and checkpoint cadence?
05:32 Speaker 6 (Marcus): Sure. Week zero access + network, week one integrate with an SDK or direct API calls, run smoke tests, validate latency  and correctness on sampling prompts; week two increase load and run canary rollout to production; after success we do a handoff to CSM for ops cadence. We'll align on success criteria up front — typically quality thresholds, cost per 1k tokens, and latency p95.
06:00 Speaker 2 (Priya): Our success criteria: 90% of responses should meet our intent match metric, p95 < 300ms for our long-form prompts, and cost under $X per 1k tokens.
06:13 Speaker 1 (Avery): We'll capture that and factor into the benchmark plan.
06:18 Speaker 3 (Lindsey): On canaries, how do rollbacks work? Is there automatic fallback to a smaller model?
06:25 Speaker 7 (Dana): We support automatic fallback policies. If latency or error rate breaches SLO, the router can switch to a compatible variant or a hosted fallback. Canary windows and traffic percentages are configurable.
06:41 Speaker 5 (Rashid): Any SOC2 or compliance paperwork we should expect?
06:47 Speaker 6 (Marcus): We'll share SOC2 Type II summary and the security pack; it includes our SAML/SSO patterns, RBAC examples, audit log samples, and KMS integration notes.
06:58 Speaker 5 (Rashid): Good — please send that to security@ggs.io.
07:03 Speaker 1 (Avery): Noted.
07:08 Speaker 2 (Priya): Any known limitations in the runtime around very long context windows? We have a use case with 50k tokens in a conversation history.
07:18 Speaker 7 (Dana): We support long-context models but with tradeoffs; for very long contexts we recommend KV cache strategies and chunking. Also kernel choices matter for 50k — we'll recommend model variants and quant profiles. Some customers use hybrid approach: embeddings + search to reduce immediate context length.
07:42 Speaker 4 (Ethan): For benchmarks do you want us to include production-like network latency and a staging VPC?
07:50 Speaker 6 (Marcus): Yes include staging VPC with realistic egress. Ideally run load tests from a host in the same cloud region to measure intra-region latency. We'll provide the load harness and sample prompt set.
08:06 Speaker 2 (Priya): For the sample prompts — we'll extract a 500-prompt set with sensitive data masked.
08:13 Speaker 1 (Avery): Perfect. Dana, anything to call out on instrumenting observability?
08:18 Speaker 7 (Dana): Console gives per-route token breakdowns, latency heatmaps, and an errors tab. We can add tracing hooks — send us the service names and we'll provide trace IDs. Also we have regressions alerting tied to eval sets.
08:36 Speaker 2 (Priya): Love that.
08:39 Speaker 3 (Lindsey): Question from my infra lead — do you require specific instance families for dedicated?
08:46 Speaker 6 (Marcus): We prefer A100 or H100 for highest throughput; for cost-optimized we use smaller GPU families with quantized models. We'll include recommended instance types in the deck.
08:58 Speaker 4 (Ethan): Is there a trial period for dedicated or is that a commit?
09:04 Speaker 6 (Marcus): Dedicated is usually a reservation, but we do short term pilot capacity in some cases — we can discuss flexible commit terms with sales.
09:14 Speaker 1 (Avery): We'll get you the sales brief after this call.
09:19 Speaker 2 (Priya): Anything about prompt safety? We have internal compliance around hallucinations.
09:26 Speaker 7 (Dana): We recommend prompt engineering patterns and system message scaffolding. Also our Optimize tool flags quality regressions and can tie alerts to prompt evaluation sets.
09:41 Speaker 5 (Rashid): On SSO — we use SAML with SCIM groups. Is SCIM supported?
09:49 Speaker 6 (Marcus): Yes, SCIM provisioning is supported. We'll share the SAML metadata and the SCIM endpoints in the security pack.
09:58 Speaker 4 (Ethan): Great. Quick note — do you expose token-level cost via the API for internal chargebacks?
10:06 Speaker 7 (Dana): Yes per-request token counts and cost estimates are in the Console and available via the usage API.
10:14 Speaker 1 (Avery): Okay wrapping up in the next 10 minutes, let's confirm action owners and dates.
10:21 Speaker 6 (Marcus): Action log: Avery will send the playbook and sample network diagram by 8/20, Dana will prepare the benchmark plan and sample prompts by 8/25, Ethan will provide CIDRs by 8/23, Rashid will send compliance questions by 8/22. Benchmark week Sep 6-10 pending signoff.
10:45 Speaker 2 (Priya): One small ask — can you include a side-by-side cost/latency matrix for the model variants?
10:52 Speaker 7 (Dana): Yes we'll include estimated cost curves and quant profiles.
11:00 Speaker 1 (Avery): Anything else from Gossamer?
11:05 Speaker 3 (Lindsey): No that's it.
11:08 Speaker 5 (Rashid): No.
11:10 Speaker 2 (Priya): Thanks everyone.
11:13 Speaker 1 (Avery): Thanks all, we'll follow up via email with the pack and calendar invites for the benchmark week and the next sync.
11:22 Speaker 6 (Marcus): Closing notes — links: onboarding playbook (drive): https://drive.redwood.example/onboarding/gossamer-playbook, security pack: https://redwood.example/security/gossamer, benchmark template: https://redwood.example/benchmarks/template.
11:38 Speaker 1 (Avery): Meeting adjourned.

Notes about transcript: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "quantisization" instead of quantization, "kay vee cache" for KV cache) present; some speaker tags are generic but participants confirmed actions verbally.
